clue.text: Depressed? Do cocaine before farewell

indicators.note: before places the cocaine letter ahead of the word for farewell

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, to con them
C is the drug-slang abbreviation for cocaine
ave is Latin for hail or farewell

explanation.surface: A reckless suggestion to take cocaine before saying goodbye, prompted by feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed?' looks like a mood, but the question mark flags its other sense: sunken or dished, as a surface can be.
explanation.definitionFit: A depressed surface is hollowed inward, which is exactly the shape of a lens or bowl curving in.

clue.text: Catches case of Columbo with 'one more thing'

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of Columbo are kept

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is one more thing added after a letter ends; also Columbo's catchphrase

explanation.surface: Columbo nails his suspect with his trademark parting question, 'just one more thing'.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbo was the scruffy TV detective, played by Peter Falk, famous for turning back with 'just one more thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop someone is slang for to catch or nab them, as police do with a suspect.

clue.text: Show respect for late 'disheveled' Peter Falk on a broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered widely, like seed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A tribute to the late Peter Falk, the scruffy actor, aired on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheveled' sits in quotes as a nod to Columbo's rumpled raincoat, but it is fodder, not the anagram signal; 'broadcast' is.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb urges courtesy toward people who have died, so following it shows respect for those lately departed.

clue.text: Do search in the centre with others

indicators.note: in the centre asks for only the middle letters of the word search

parts.note: the rest means the others, those remaining

explanation.surface: Police instructions: carry out a search, central area, along with the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is police slang: to be done for something is to be arrested or charged.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, police who do a suspect nick or take them into custody.

clue.text: Conclusion, say, to cover news about investigator

indicators.note: to cover means the example abbreviation wraps around the rest

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: about means the two Ns sit either side of the investigator

parts.note: news read as plural of N, the abbreviation for new, gives two Ns
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: The final part of a news story about a detective, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is 'news' read as plural 'new': two Ns, not a bulletin. 'to cover' and 'about' are both containment signals, nested one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclusion is the end or close of something, such as a story's final scene.

clue.text: Grows into suits

definitions.meaning: a caterpillar grows into a butterfly: it turns into one
a colour suits you when it flatters or looks right on you

explanation.surface: A boy grows into his suits as he gets older.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two senses: to turn into something over time, and to look fitting on someone.

clue.text: Being spiteful is beginning to be irritating

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the word be is taken

parts.note: something itching is irritating the skin

explanation.surface: A remark that malice is starting to grate on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Malicious complaining and backbiting about others is informally called this, a spiteful sniping.

clue.text: Covers preserve work that is special

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
op, short for opus, is a musical work
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Instructions for bottling fruit, a special job, then putting lids on.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopies are overhead shelters of cloth or foliage, things that cover from above.

clue.text: Drug satisfied husband in the morning, dear, keeping hard with a source of supply

parts.note: to meet a demand is to satisfy it; met is the past tense
a.m. means in the morning

indicators.note: keeping means the endearment holds the next letter within it

parts.note: pet is an affectionate name, like dear
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a mine is a rich source, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: A tale of a contented husband, sweetheart and a dealer's supply of a hard drug in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal meth is a powerful stimulant narcotic, illegal in most countries.

clue.text: They murder visitors around lake

indicators.note: around means the word for visitors goes around the lake letter

parts.note: strangers are people from elsewhere, visitors
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Killers loose among tourists near a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Throttlers kill by choking, so these are people who murder with their hands or a cord.

clue.text: Person covering ground, state policeman initially going in front

indicators.note: going in front puts the policeman's letter ahead of the word for state
initially means only the first letter of the word policeman is wanted

parts.note: to aver is to state or assert

explanation.surface: A policeman on the beat leads the way while covering ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering ground' suggests patrolling, but it is literal: laying slabs over earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who lays flagstones or tarmac literally covers the ground with a hard surface.

clue.text: One could go off with detective working around schedule

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: around means the word for schedule is turned round

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: A detective on duty rearranging his timetable might just snap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' hints at a temper or a person leaving, but means explode.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is a device that sets off a bomb, so it is one thing that could explode.

clue.text: Can churchman approach sin? Characters inside clink set free

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order, so they are rearranged
the characters inside a word are those left when its two ends are taken away

explanation.surface: A question whether a cleric may go near sin, then a prisoner released from jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is US slang for prison, and CLINK is British slang for jail too; LIN, the inside of clink, joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to a jail ministers to inmates, and can is slang for jail.

clue.text: Subordinate to screen detective might work like this?

parts.note: to be under someone is to be subordinate to them
to cover something is to screen or shield it

explanation.surface: A junior officer covering for a TV detective, wondering how he operates.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer in disguise, posing as someone else, works incognito to infiltrate criminal circles.

clue.text: Casually sleep with English scruff

parts.note: a nap is a short, informal sleep

explanation.surface: An unkempt Englishman dozing off in a relaxed way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruff' looks like a scruffy person, but it is the scruff of the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, the part by which a cat lifts a kitten.

clue.text: Peril not unusual for crime fighters

indicators.note: unusual signals an odd, irregular arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Danger is routine for those who fight crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The international police organisation coordinates forces across countries against cross-border criminals.

clue.text: They join police with round going off: run in two seconds

indicators.note: in means the run sits inside the two seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, so two of them make SS

indicators.note: going off means the round letter departs from police

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A recruit joins the police force, the patrol leaves, and he runs for two seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Splicing is joining ropes, film or tape end to end, so these are people or tools that join.

clue.text: Recover arm: solve murders

indicators.note: read as re-cover, putting the letters back in a new arrangement, it signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A detective's work: recover the weapon and solve the killings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recover' looks like part of the detective's to-do list, but it signals the rearrangement of ARM SOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: In gangster euphemism, getting rid of a person is their removal, so killings are taken as removals.

clue.text: Former lover with big bosom, essentially models

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means large or generous

indicators.note: essentially means the central letter, the heart, of the word bosom

explanation.surface: An ex with a large bust is, at heart, a model.
explanation.definitionFit: Models in the sense of patterns to copy are instances or specimens held up to follow.

clue.text: Like No Time to Die

indicators.note: No means the time letter is missing from the word for die

parts.note: to peter out is to fade away and die

explanation.surface: A comparison with the Bond film No Time to Die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No Time to Die' reads as the film title, but it splits into an instruction: remove T from PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun 'like', as in 'you and your like', is an equal, someone of the same rank.

clue.text: Plain or flash coat for detective on street?

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the detective's letters above the street

parts.note: in a flash means in a mo, a moment

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Is Columbo's coat plain or showy for walking the streets?
explanation.definitionFit: Unassuming and simple, without show, is a fair synonym for plain, as in a plain, unpretentious house.

clue.text: Detective with charge that's appropriate

parts.note: PI is a private investigator
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A private eye with a fee that's suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like the adjective 'fitting', but it is the verb: to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take without permission, which is what a copier of films or a sea robber does.

clue.text: Icon Columbo's back with cigar: mill around like his character?

indicators.note: to mill around is to move about aimlessly, signalling the letters are stirred up
the back of a word is its final letter, here the end of the name Columbo

explanation.surface: The iconic detective, cigar in hand, wanders around a crime scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbo always had a cigar; the question mark admits his character is a crime-solver rather than a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: His character studies crime and criminals, so is aptly described with the adjective for the study of crime.

clue.text: Watch out for intellect

definitions.meaning: to watch out for a step is to be careful of it
the intellect is the thinking faculty, the brain

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for taking care about something and a noun for the reasoning faculty.

clue.text: Foe messed with lieutenant's head, TV ace making U-turn

indicators.note: letters messed with are jumbled up into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An enemy tampers with an officer's mind, and a TV star does a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or policy, borrowed from French, is a figurative about-turn.

clue.text: Defence of Italy twice cut ball out

indicators.note: out signals letters knocked out of place and rearranged
twice means the Italy letter is used two times

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: cut means a letter is lopped off the end of ball

explanation.surface: An Italian football defence twice cuts the ball out of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims ball to BAL; with II (Italy twice) those letters are rearranged by 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect's claim to have been elsewhere at the time of a crime is their standard legal defence.

clue.text: Turns down rubbish song's intro

parts.note: refuse is household rubbish, trash

indicators.note: a song's intro is its opening, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A DJ rejects a track because its opening is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline an offer or request is to reject it, saying no.

clue.text: See 2
